sections.skill: Order and justify the steps of proofs about angles formed by intersecting and parallel lines

questions.prompt: Lines meet at a point, forming angle 1 and angle 2 as vertical angles, and angle 3 next to both (angle 3 forms a linear pair with angle 1 and with angle 2). Put the steps of the proof that angle 1 = angle 2 in a correct order. (Two orders are correct.)

items.text: angle 1 + angle 3 = angle 2 + angle 3 (both sums equal 180 degrees)
angle 1 = angle 2 (subtract angle 3 from both sides)

questions.correct_answer: angle 1 + angle 3 = 180 degrees (linear pair) → angle 2 + angle 3 = 180 degrees (linear pair) → angle 1 + angle 3 = angle 2 + angle 3 (both sums equal 180 degrees) → angle 1 = angle 2 (subtract angle 3 from both sides)

sections.relationship: Harder: the perpendicular bisector theorem and converses.
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: M is the midpoint of segment AB, and line PM is perpendicular to AB, so P is on the perpendicular bisector of AB. Put the steps of the proof that PA = PB in a correct order. (Two orders are correct.)

items.text: AM = BM, and angles PMA and PMB are right angles (midpoint; perpendicular)
Triangle PMA is congruent to triangle PMB (SAS)
PA = PB (corresponding parts of congruent triangles)

questions.correct_answer: AM = BM, and angles PMA and PMB are right angles (midpoint; perpendicular) → PM = PM (a segment equals itself) → Triangle PMA is congruent to triangle PMB (SAS) → PA = PB (corresponding parts of congruent triangles)

questions.prompt: Theorem: a point is on the perpendicular bisector of AB exactly when it is the same distance from A and B. Point P has PA = PB = 7. What follows?

choices.text: P is the midpoint of AB.
P is on the perpendicular bisector of AB.

questions.correct_answer: P is on the perpendicular bisector of AB.

Put the steps of the proof that angle 4 + angle 6 = 180 degrees when p is parallel to q in a correct order. (Two orders are correct.)

items.text: angle 4 = angle 5 (alternate interior angles, p parallel to q)
angle 4 + angle 6 = 180 degrees (substitute angle 4 for angle 5)

questions.correct_answer: angle 4 = angle 5 (alternate interior angles, p parallel to q) → angle 5 + angle 6 = 180 degrees (linear pair) → angle 4 + angle 6 = 180 degrees (substitute angle 4 for angle 5)

Nothing; looking at the diagram is enough.
